name: Introduction and overview — Typhoon-class Submarine — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Typhoon-class Submarine
description: Introduction and overview of the Typhoon-class Submarine: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Soviet Typhoon class — six built — are the largest submarines ever constructed: 48,000 tons submerged, 574 feet long, with 20 R-39 ballistic missiles. Their multiple pressure hulls gave crews unusual comfort, including a swimming pool. One remains as a test platform; the rest were scrapped. Baseline facts: Soviet ballistic-missile submarine; 6 built; 48,000 tons; largest submarines ever..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
